Richard and Will Freedman’s stable is filled with exciting unknown youngsters without too many older stars, as they head into this spring with rebuilding in mind. Gun colt Genesis Runner headlines their Classic crop with the Spring Champion as a key target.

Coolmore sire Home Affairs currently has Timeform Australia’s top rated 3-year-old colt, Guest House, and top rated 3-year-old filly, Natural Fling. Natural Fling won a jump out at Flemington on Thursday, while last start Group winner Guest House runs in a hot G1 Golden Rose field on Saturday.

Three juvenile heats at the Flemington jump outs put more focus on first season sire Anamoe as his colt Ankaa looked impressive when winning for trainers Tony and Calvin McEvoy. They also won the first heat with Hellbent colt Silent Intent, while John McArdle’s Snitzel filly Musandam won the third heat.

Blessed Eagle led a quartet of promising 3-year-olds on Wednesday, producing a sustained display of speed at Warwick Farm, while Avery Anna, Stipulation and Chuchichaschtli advertised plenty of upside also at Warwick Farm and Geelong, respectively.
Gelagotis Racing heads into spring with a proven core of performers and also an exciting new generation of 2-year-olds coming through the Pakenham-based stable.

Yarraman Park Stud has built an elite broodmare band to support their roster, but also to help resident champion I Am Invincible become the influential broodmare sire they expect him to be. Matt Scown and Arthur Mitchell unpack which of his daughters will be going where, and what mares have earned a spot in his exclusive 2026 book.

Four 2.5% shares in Decorum, a full brother to G1 Coolmore Stud Stakes winner Switzerland, sold for $30,000 each in this week's Inglis Digital September Late Sale, placing a seven-figure value on the four-time winning gelding. Plus, Just Magic, a half-sister to Listed-winning Celerity, topped the sale when selling for $140,000.

The finishing time is only half the story for form analyst Nic Ashman, who assesses some of the performances amongst last Saturday's stakes races and whether or not they impressed him. The right race shape was key to a lot of the winners, but Ashman sees merit in some of those that weren't favoured by the pattern.
